name: sc-im
desc: Spreadsheet program for the terminal, using ncurses
why: A terminal spreadsheet with vim-style keys is a fun old-school environment, though spreadsheets are a crowded niche.

brief.what_it_is: sc-im (Spreadsheet Calculator Improvised) is an ncurses-based, vim-like spreadsheet calculator that runs in a terminal. You navigate cells with hjkl-style keys, enter numbers, text and formulas, and use vim-style commands such as :w to save. It reads CSV, tab-delimited, XLSX and ODS files (ODS import only) and writes CSV, tab-delimited, XLSX, sc-format and Markdown. It also supports Lua scripting and can be used as a non-interactive calculator that reads its input from an external script.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents sc-im as a vim-like, ncurses spreadsheet calculator derived from the original sc by James Gosling and Mark Weiser, with later mods by Chuck Martin. It does not state a broader motivation beyond that lineage.
brief.how_it_works: It is a C program built with make, using ncurses for the terminal interface and bison or yacc for its formula grammar (the repo includes doc/grammar_yacc_tools). Optional features are pulled in at build time: Lua for scripting, gnuplot for plots, libxml-2.0 and libzip for XLSX/ODS import, xlsxwriter for XLSX export, and tmux, xclip or pbpaste for clipboard. Settings are read from a scimrc file in ~/.config/sc-im.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew install is available (brew install sc-im). For a manual build you must edit src/Makefile for your system, then run make -C src, and optionally make -C src install as root. Requirements: ncurses (wide-character build preferred), bison or yacc, gcc, make, pkg-config and which. Optional extras: gnuplot, libxlsxreader (XLS read), xlsxwriter (XLSX export), libxml-2.0 and libzip (XLSX/ODS import), Lua, and threads support. On OS X, Lua scripting needs lua@5.1 specifically. For Ubuntu XLSX support and other distros or OSes, the README points to the wiki rather than giving steps. Optional config goes in ~/.config/sc-im/scimrc; the help file lists other variables.
brief.standout: It is a vim-style terminal spreadsheet with an unusually broad feature list for the niche: undo and redo, Lua scripting plus C dynamically linked modules, triggers, RGB colours, wide-character alphabets including Japanese and Chinese, and XLSX and ODS interchange. The row limit is 65,536 by default and can be raised to 1,048,576.
brief.status: Maintained, per the README. A note dated 05/21/2025 announces release v0.8.5 and says it is a one-person project. The page shows about 1,572 commits and 5.7k stars. The fetched page did not show the date of the latest commit, so recency beyond that note is unverified.
brief.caveats: Maintained by one person who asks for donations; the README says income is tight. Default row count is 65,536 and 702 columns. Full functionality depends on optional libraries, and XLSX import and export need extra packages. Lua scripting on OS X needs Lua 5.1 specifically. The manual build needs a Makefile edit. The README says the author does not know whether anyone uses the app. A Minix note says to disable autobackup and HAVE_PTHREAD there. The licence file exists but its type was not visible on the fetched page.
